Always made my best money by being early: $YFI farming, $LIT referrals etc.

Only 9 days in, and I'm not early to Papertrade anymore.

Early farmers got 100 PAPER per $1 of eligible losses. Now just ~11.

Just feels like I'm an exit liquidity. No?

A $1000 losing trade now gets me ~10.7k PAPER. 

Stake it and I'd get ~$2.60 to $4.90 per day if recent payouts continued.

200 to 385 days just to recover my loss. And that excludes new issuance diluting my share.

So once PAPER becomes transferable, some traders might prefer selling to recover losses instead of waiting for yield.

Soooo... The BIG BET on PAPER is whether traders keep gambling after farming stops making sense.

At the end, the product needs to be worth using even when the incentives aren't enough.

For losers, yeah, they get the token.

But winners pay an 'asymmetric-impact haircut' BEFORE the additional 2% fee. 

(There are no funding or notional trading fees, so the cost comparison isn't so simple)

How many are here for the product vs deliberately losing because they expect PAPER to pay them back?

That is what one needs to answer.

As Galaxy Research posted:

'Once PAPER becomes transferable, the market price will determine how much farming happens, and that, in turn, will determine long-term revenue.'

So PAPER dumping could mean less farming -> lower payouts -> less reason to hold.

Got rekt from this kind of down spiral a few times.

My next opportunity might be buying from farmers selling to recover losses.

But only if the price makes sense on payouts AFTER farming slows.

So I will treat PAPER as a "revenue token" if it sustains it after a while.

Trading PAPER once it's transferable seems easier to me than trading on Papertrade itself.

Can institutional-grade vaults become a core part of the future of DeFi?

Here are some of my thoughts ↓

Lending vault deposits have grown from $1.5B to $10B in just two years.

I think trading vaults could be 10x bigger than that.

The idea is pretty simple:

Instead of institutions building their own trading infrastructure or managing every position themselves, they could allocate capital to experienced traders through onchain vaults.

You'd essentially get professional capital management with transparent positions, predefined risk, and the ability to monitor what's happening live with your money.

Some projects like @Infinit_Labs are already building serious infra for this vision. For example, INFINIT OS already combines AI tools and the infrastructure needed to research and operate a trading vault

Their first vault (APEX MS) is already running on @HyperliquidX and outperformed $BTC in the last 60 days.

What other protocols are building towards this?

LMK what I should research next.

Just focus on crypto. It has its own timeline, and you have no edge in equities/macro.

There will be always be something that drags out the emotions in you, and there will always be a strong case for a market crash. Just look at the plethora of people/accounts that have made it their life's work to incorrectly call secular bear markets.

Outside of the 0-1 correlation events crypto has its own cycle. It tops and bottoms irrespective of equities/macro. People say it front runs it or whatever, but the fact remains that it has its own timeline. 

TOTAL is currently above the May highs, above its 10W EMA, 20W MA & 10M EMA (which historically supports a bull market all the way up). There was that big impulse off the bottom which you see at the end of bear markets, and now we are at that sticky area where everyone with PTSD gets shaken out before eventually going higher.

BTC is looking better than alt coins, which got overstretched. Bitcoin has been shaking off insane amounts of bad news that if we were still in a bear market would have taken us way way down (additional signal alongside the chart). That doesn't mean we can't still shake out more tourists here.

There is a lot of room to go down and remain HTF bullish with the trend still in our favour. 

In early 2023 we had the USDC depeg which shook everyone out but we were still in a bull market, as the market structure had shifted. That time around we hit the 200D MA (~72k currently) before moving up. 

I believe we are here now, and we can still have annoying chop for a while with more people attempting longs and shorts at the wrong time. 

TOTAL2/TOTAL3 remains 37% & 30% off their 2021 ATHs. If you don't think we surpass those market caps then you should find another asset class to spend your time on.  

It is simply impossible for me to be bearish when the industry has made so much progress and we are this far away from where we were 5 years ago. We have clear evidence of an acceleration of institutional adoption and tradfi bringing all assets onchain. 

We already have our dot com crash behind us, and good alt coins are rather under owned globally relative to all other asset classes. We have tailwinds, with equities having more defined headwinds. This remains the opportunity, and patience is required.

The only way to fuck this up is to be too zoomed thinking you can time macro consistently with Dunning Kruger syndrome because you had a good crypto cycle once, or being overly cautious because you have PTSD and can't fathom anything going right for you.

Stop trying to control everything, and just let go.

Last major $SIVE disclosure was 100M CW DFB laser capacity Q4 2027. And a new foundry partner (that makes 2 including Win Semi).

Expected $JBL revenue coming in H1 2027 (with lasers for Jabil's 1.6T LRO scaling up H2 2027).

There's channel checks along the way like CIOE where Sivers was engaged with Chinese pluggable makers + laser ASPs being raised.

70mW/100mW ranges were the most tight to Chinese pluggable makers, which was surprising.

Biggest industry read through was $LITE selling out into 2029, making agreements for 2030, and having hyperscalers pay for capacity expansion for 2031. 

I don't think anyone has enough information to do any sort of accurate modeling for $SIVE like you can for $AAOI given they don't release product breakdown + capacity targets by quarter.

The 200mW NPO lasers Sivers is sampling is likely different ASP than your 70mW lasers shipped to pluggable makers. And your custom CPO lasers are different pricing too. 

Like all sampling/qualification players from $AEHR to $AAOI back in 2025, usually the risk/reward comes in whether qualifications convert and what new customers they have, which is always a risk. 

In a bull case, if $SIVE comes online with 300m laser supply (2:1 implied ratio, already has "tremendous" supply online from likely US fab) during a structural shortage.  

Pluggable players like $JBL, 6 other vendors.  

$GFS as the reference design laser for their CPO/NPO platform. 

Your minor players vendors like $POET, $AEVA and other players end up scaling.

And all the other custom products they hinted they were working on in the past for CPO years back.  

I think the probability that they cook is higher since there's so many ongoing qualifications during a bottleneck. 

We've already seen ownership changes from Swedish investors to US/International retail from $SIVE shareholder disclosures. 

My guess is that trends institutional from retail before US listing next year amid the market correction. 

Think people forgot institutions have already financed their expansion, which was a 700M SEK round 100%+ ago (multiple times oversubscribed). 

And that $SIVE uses primarily external fabs, so it's not the same as a lot of the major financing concerns affecting Neoclouds. 

Anyway, up to management execution, I'm not running Sivers so no clue what other companies are working with them now, whether it's Cambridge or some other US player like Semtec.

TLDR:

- Just need to wait for earnings for more disclosures around qualifications + partners, only so much public can guess from channel checks and supplier mapping. 

Not quite the same as $LITE CEO where you can see the guy on Fox news or Bloomberg interviews every week (which is a good thing)

⚡ DAILY METALS PULSE — OCTOBER 19, 2026 ⚡

Four metals. One pulse. No noise.

A new week begins with a fascinating setup.

Oil is retreating. Treasury yields are easing. China just reported better-than-expected GDP growth.

And precious metals are finally showing some life after a brutal correction.

Here’s what I’m watching. 👇

☢️ URANIUM — THE QUIET ACCUMULATION

The spot market remains relatively quiet around $90/lb.

But look beneath the surface.

Reported uranium term contracting has reached approximately 77.7 million pounds in 2026, compared with just 44 million at the same point last year.

That’s a 77% increase!

Meanwhile, Kazatomprom shareholders approved another uranium sale to China while rejecting a proposed Russian supply deal.

India wants to double domestic uranium production.

And Western enrichment capacity continues expanding.

The competition for secure nuclear fuel is becoming increasingly strategic.

⚡ COPPER — CHINA DELIVERS

China’s Q3 GDP growth came in at 4.5%, slightly exceeding expectations.

Meanwhile, copper continues trading near historically elevated levels.

Mine disruptions in Chile, constrained concentrate availability and tight inventories remain important concerns.

But there’s another story developing.

Investors are questioning whether the enormous AI infrastructure spending boom can continue at its current pace.

That’s worth watching.

Because copper’s next move may depend on whether improving Chinese demand can outweigh concerns about technology-sector investment.

Longer term?

New copper mines still take YEARS to develop.

🥈 SILVER — THE COMEBACK CANDIDATE?

Silver has suffered a devastating correction, ending Friday near $57/oz.

More than 50% below January’s record.

But something interesting is happening underneath.

Indian silver ETF inflows surged approximately 55% in September.

SLV added roughly 3.7 million ounces during the latest reported week.

And the Silver Institute still forecasts a SIXTH consecutive annual supply deficit.

Yes, solar manufacturers are reducing silver consumption per cell.

And COMEX inventories have recently recovered.

But if investment demand continues strengthening while interest-rate expectations ease, silver could become VERY interesting again.

🥇 GOLD — THE MACRO PENDULUM SWINGS

Gold is starting Monday around $4,180, up approximately 0.4%.

What’s changed?

The US decision to ease certain Russian oil sanctions has pushed oil futures lower.

Lower oil prices could reduce inflation pressure.

Lower inflation expectations could mean less aggressive Fed tightening.

And lower Treasury yields are already helping gold.

But geopolitical risks remain elevated, and central-bank demand continues supporting the longer-term thesis.

Gold’s correction has been painful.

Its monetary role hasn’t disappeared.

🔥 WHAT I’M WATCHING THIS WEEK

☢️ Uranium — Utility contracting and the gap between quiet spot activity and stronger term demand.

⚡ Copper — China’s economic momentum, mine disruptions and AI-related capital spending.

🥈 Silver — ETF inflows, COMEX inventories and whether the precious-metals rebound gains traction.

🥇 Gold — Treasury yields, oil prices and expectations ahead of the Fed’s October 27–28 meeting.

THE BIG PICTURE

The market is increasingly separating short-term financial conditions from long-term commodity fundamentals.

Higher rates can punish metals.

Economic slowdowns can temporarily reduce demand.

But neither creates new uranium deposits, copper mines or silver production overnight.

And gold remains insurance against a world struggling with debt, inflation and geopolitical uncertainty.

Four metals.

Four different catalysts.

One increasingly interesting final quarter of 2026.

The volatility is real. So are the opportunities. 🔥

The reason is that precompiles and EVM both operate on data that has to be included into the ethereum chain somehow, which realistically means included in a block as calldata. That space is limited - even with PeerDAS and blocks-in-blobs, there's a practical cap of ~8 MB/s before it starts getting uncomfortable.

Remember: it's not a blockchain. It's a cryptographic world computer. Any data/computation that does not need to be in the "main thread" of data/execution should not be put into the main thread.

This way everyone can use whatever cryptography they want, the Ethereum chain can be lean, and we never need to add more precompiles again.
